question: When you see this traffic sign, you should
picture: Red rectangular sign on a post with white text "REDUCE SPEED NOW"

options.text: Slow down on seeing the sign.
Reduce speed after the sign.
Keep within the speed limit of the road.

question: This red signal light before the tunnel means
picture: Black lane signal panel with two unlit white circles and a red X on the right

options.text: Possible obstruction ahead, be prepared to change lane.
The said lane is closed to traffic.
Light out of order. Proceed with caution.

question: When you see this sign, you
picture: Red triangle warning sign with a black pedestrian walking over a zebra crossing

options.text: Should slow down and be prepared to stop for pedestrians to cross the road.
Need not slow down if there is no pedestrian at the Crossing.
Should sound your horn to warn the pedestrians of your approach.

notes: Option B capitalises 'Crossing' mid-sentence as printed.

question: When you see this sign, you should
picture: Red triangle warning sign with two black child figures running hand in hand

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully, beware of children crossing the road.
Drive at the normal speed as the jogging track is on the opposite side of the road.
Keep a lookout for a children playground ahead.

notes: Option C reads 'a children playground' as printed.

question: What does a single yellow zig-zag line by the side of the road mean?
picture: Top-down view of a road with a single yellow zig-zag line along the left edge

options.text: No waiting except for the immediate picking up and letting down of passengers.
Allowed to wait as long as the driver remains in the car.
No stopping at all times.

question: Are you allowed to alight passengers along the road with double yellow zig-zag lines?
picture: Top-down view of a road with double yellow zig-zag lines along the left edge

options.text: Yes.
No, except Sundays and Public Holidays.
No.

question: Which of these traffic lights mean 'Go' for straight and right turn vehicles?

options.text: Traffic light showing a full green light plus an amber right-turn arrow lit
Traffic light showing a full green light plus a red right-turn arrow lit
Traffic light showing a full green light plus a green right-turn arrow lit

question: When approaching a traffic light signal that has turned to amber, you should

options.text: Speed up.
Maintain your speed.
Slow down and stop.

question: When the amber traffic light is flashing continuously, you should

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Stop and wait for it to change to green.
Drive through it quickly.

question: When the 'amber' traffic light signal is flashing, you should

options.text: Carry on driving.
Slow down and look out for other vehicles before proceeding.

question: The signal of this policeman means vehicles approaching:
picture: Traffic policeman in white uniform and helmet facing forward with both arms down at his sides

options.text: On his right and left to stop.
From his front and behind to go.
On his right and left to go.

picture: Traffic policeman in white uniform shown side-on with one arm raised straight up, palm open

options.text: On his right, front and behind to stop.
On his left to stop.
On his right to get ready to stop.

question: Which of these driver's arm signal mean he intends to slow down ?

Rear view of a car with the driver's arm out of the right window and orange circular motion lines
Rear view of a car with the driver's arm out of the right window and short orange up-down motion marks

Reduce your speed and assist the rider to overtake safely.
Ignore the rider and continue driving at your normal speed.

question: When another vehicle is overtaking you, you should

options.text: Not speed up but assist him to overtake.
Change lane and keep to the right.
Increase your speed gradually.
